{{Short description|Theorem}}
In mathematics, the '''Andreotti–Grauert theorem''', introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Andreotti|last2=Grauert|author1-link=Aldo Andreotti|author2-link=Hans Grauert|year=1962}},  gives conditions for [[cohomology group]]s of [[coherent sheaf|coherent sheaves]] over [[complex manifold]]s to vanish or to be finite-dimensional.

==Statement==

Let {{mvar|X}} be a (not necessarily [[Reduced ring|reduced]]) [[complex analytic space]], and <math>\mathcal{F}</math> a coherent analytic sheaf over X. Then,

* <math>\rm{dim}_{\mathbb{C}} \; H^i (X, \mathcal{F}) < \infty</math> for <math>i \geq q</math> (resp. <math>i < \rm{codh} \; (\mathcal{F}) - q</math>), if {{mvar|X}} is q-pseudoconvex (resp. q-pseudoconcave). (finiteness)<ref>{{harv|Andreotti|Grauert|1962|loc=THÉORÈME 14.}}</ref><ref name=Ohsawa1984>{{harv|Ohsawa1984}}</ref>
* <math>H^i (X, \mathcal{F}) = 0</math> for <math>i \geq q</math>, if {{mvar|X}} is q-complete. (vanish)<ref>{{harv|Andreotti|Grauert|1962|loc=COROLLAIRE.}}</ref>{{R|Ohsawa1984}}
